title: Overnight Baked French Toast
subtitle: cinnamon custard-soaked bread under a buttery brown sugar crust, ready to bake
imageAlt: A golden baked French toast casserole with a caramelized brown sugar top, one portion on a cream plate with maple syrup and a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 9×13 dish: brunch for two, plus 4 more

beforeYouStart.text: Soak it at least 4 hours or overnight in the fridge.
Day-old crusty bread holds its shape best.

items.name: loaf crusty bread
items.note: about 450 g, day-old, torn in 3 cm pieces

steps.title: Fill the dish
steps.text: Butter a 23×33 cm (9×13 in) baking dish and pile in the bread.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and salt. Pour evenly over the bread and press it down.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, or overnight.

steps.title: Top and bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Stir the melted butter, brown sugar and cinnamon together and drizzle over the top. Bake uncovered 45–50 minutes, until puffed, golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes and serve with warm maple syrup.

fixIt.fix: Bake 10 minutes more, tented with foil, until 74°C (165°F).
Tent loosely with foil after 30 minutes.
Use crusty bread rather than soft sandwich bread, and tear, don't cube.

saleTip: No Frills bakery marks day-old loaves down in the evening; perfect for this.
swap: Challah or brioche for crusty bread. Half-and-half for some of the milk.
leftovers: Reheat squares in the toaster oven for a crisp top.
doneness: Egg dishes to 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested overnight French toast casserole methods (Canadian Living, Allrecipes test kitchen): torn day-old bread soaked in a cinnamon custard, topped with butter and brown sugar and baked at 175°C.
prepAhead: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead; add the topping just before baking.
reheat: Covered in the microwave 1–2 minutes, or at 180°C (350°F) for 12 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Cinnamon French toast bake with syrup; no crumble top.

stepNotes.3: Basic: skip the topping; just bake.

fancy.note: Berries baked on top and a dusting of icing sugar.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: scatter the berries over the top before the crumble.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: dust with icing sugar through a sieve.

plating: Scoop, don't slice, for the craggy top.

why.0-1: Crusty bread soaks up the custard and keeps a little chew.
why.1-1: The brown sugar and butter top bakes into a crackly crust.

funFact: French toast is far older than France: a Roman cookbook from about the 4th century soaks bread in milk and egg and fries it.
drink: Hot coffee with cream, or cold milk.
